[FORM:sonnet] Write about rewriting a rough draft into clear argument.

a working bridge from doubt to chosen aim.

[FORM:sonnet] Write about rewriting a rough draft into clear argument.

I keep one narrow window lit at last,
while rewriting and rough drift beyond the pane.
The noisy tabs that mocked me have gone past,
their glitter traded for a useful strain.
I cut the swollen draft to nerve and bone,
and watch the argument stand clean and spare.
A thesis learns to carry weight alone,
not dressed in borrowed thunder, only care.
The cursor blinks like rain against the glass,
a metronome that keeps my breathing true.
I choose one road and let the others pass,
accepting what a finite hour can do.
By morning, effort hardens into light;
the page is less afraid, and so am I.

[FORM:sonnet] Write about choosing one path and accepting tradeoffs.

I keep one narrow window lit at last,
while choosing and path drift beyond the pane.
The noisy tabs that mocked me have gone past,
their glitter traded for a useful strain.

and watch the argument stand clean and spare.
A thesis learns to carry weight alone,

[FORM:sonnet] Write about rewriting a rough draft into clear argument.

At midnight I close every glittering door,
and leave one task alive beneath the lamp.
The room is bare, the floorboards keep the score,
a thin and honest silence, dry and damp.
I carve excess from every stubborn claim,
until the paragraph can stand and breathe.
No borrowed smoke, no ornamental flame,
just clear connective tissue underneath.
My coffee cools; the keyboard answers rain.
The sentence turns, then settles into place.
I trade my appetite for easy gain
for patient cuts and one deliberate pace.
When dawn arrives, the draft is finally plain:
a working bridge from doubt to chosen aim.
